# Studienstiftung: Summary
The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes, founded in Dresden in 1925, is Germany's principal scholarship foundation supporting highly talented students and doctoral candidates. After dissolution under National Socialism in 1934, it was refounded as an association in Cologne in 1948. Its presidents and secretary generals have included notable figures such as Adolf Grimme, Manfred Eigen, Reinhard Zimmermann, and Michael Hoch.
The Studienstiftung awards general and specialized scholarships to undergraduates, graduates, and PhD students studying full time at universities in Germany, the EU, or Switzerland. Financial support includes monthly allowances (up to €855 for students, up to €1,650 for PhDs from October 2025), additional insurance, child support, and tax-free status. Academic support features summer schools, research, mentorship, and subsidized conferences. Admission prioritizes “excellence, initiative, and responsibility,” using school and professor nominations, competition winners, assessment tests, and alumni recommendations, with no fixed admissions quota. In 2023, 14,888 scholars were supported (0.48% of German students), and 93.5% received approved requests for continued funding. The Studienstiftung has produced many prominent alumni across science, business, arts, politics, and journalism.
